meta.title: Operation of Deep Freezer in Pharmacology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To store biological samples, drug solutions, serum, plasma, tissue homogenates, and heat-labile reference standards at −20°C or −80°C to prevent degradation during long-term storage in the Pharmacology laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for long-term preservation of biological specimens, sera, plasma samples, stock drug solutions, and biochemical assay reagents requiring sub-zero temperature storage.
procedure: Set the deep freezer to the required temperature: −20°C for most biological samples and drug stock solutions; −80°C for long-term storage of enzymes, nucleic acids, and plasma proteins.
Allow the unit to reach and stabilize at the set temperature before loading samples — verify with an internal calibrated thermometer or built-in display.
Label all samples before storage: sample name/ID, concentration, date, experimenter, and study/project number.
Store samples in appropriately sealed cryogenic tubes or polypropylene tubes — never use glass at −80°C (glass cracks).
Group and organize samples in labelled freezer boxes: one box per experiment or per date.
Maintain an inventory log: record sample ID, storage date, freezer location (rack-box-position), and volume.
Segregate samples by category: reference standards, experimental samples, biological specimens.
Monitor temperature daily and record in the temperature monitoring log.
Set up temperature alarms — alert level: −15°C for −20°C units; −70°C for −80°C units.
In case of power failure: do not open the freezer; a properly sealed deep freezer maintains temperature for 4–8 hours without power.
Defrost the unit when ice build-up exceeds 2 cm or as per manufacturer schedule — transfer samples to a backup freezer during defrosting.
After defrosting, clean interior with mild disinfectant and dry completely before restarting.
Record all temperature deviations and corrective actions taken in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Never store food in the laboratory deep freezer — risk of accidental ingestion and contamination.
Wear insulated cryogenic gloves when accessing −80°C material — contact frostbite occurs rapidly.
Allow samples taken from −80°C to thaw at −20°C first, then on ice — direct room-temperature thawing degrades labile components.
Do not store aerosols, flammable solvents, or reactive chemicals in the deep freezer.
Ensure the power supply to the deep freezer is on a priority/UPS circuit — power failure causes catastrophic sample loss.
Do not use the deep freezer as a step to reach upper shelves — overloading the door and compressor vibration disrupts temperature.
Clean condenser coils every 6 months to maintain cooling efficiency.
